topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the course structure, her background, and the key learning outcomes regarding environmental carcinogens and cancer causation.

topics.label: Cancer Causation: Genetic Chance versus Environmental Exposures
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the fundamental concepts of cancer development, debating whether it arises from endogenous 'bad luck' mutations or environmental exposures using global epidemiological data.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Cancer Etiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how various pathogens cause cancer, highlighting Burkitt lymphoma and the interaction between EBV, malaria, and genetic translocation as a case study.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens: Activation and DNA Damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore specific chemical and physical carcinogens, explaining how xenobiotic metabolism, bulky adducts, and radiation directly or indirectly damage DNA.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Chronic Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish cancer initiators from promoters, describing the role of inflammation, the Berenbaum two-stage model, and tissue- or developmental-stage vulnerability.

topics.label: Methods for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental approaches used to detect and prove the carcinogenicity of environmental substances.
